title: CHAPTER 8: HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN BANKING

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Human Resource Structure in Indian Public Sector Banks operates under guidelines prescribed by the Ministry of Finance and individual bank boards.
The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) functions as an autonomous body conducting standardized recruitment for PO, Clerk, and Specialist Officer cadres.
Wage revisions and service conditions for bank employees are settled through periodic Bipartite Settlements negotiated by the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) and employee unions.
Modern banking relies heavily on HR Metrics and Analytics, utilizing key indicators like Revenue per Employee, Cost per Hire, and Attrition Rate to optimize workforce performance.

blocks.content: Human Resource Management in banking is transforming from traditional personnel administration to strategic workforce analytics and talent management.

blocks.content: Important: IBA (Indian Banks' Association) negotiates on behalf of management with employee unions (AIBEA, AIBOA, INBEF, etc.). Settlements are bipartite and generally apply to all member banks.

items: Bipartite Settlements for wage revisions in PSBs are negotiated for a 5-year tenure between IBA and United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU).
Interview rounds are conducted for Officers (Scale-I and above) recruited through IBPS, whereas interviews are completely abolished for Clerical cadre posts.
Key HR productivity metrics frequently asked in exams include 'Revenue per Employee' and 'Net Profit per Employee'.
